english.notes:
(i) These regulations apply to persons driving a bus on or after 10th September 2008 or driving a lorry on or after 10th September 2009.
(ii) "Relevant vehicle" means a vehicle for which is required a driving licence of category C, C+E, D or D+E as defined in Article 3(1) of the Driving Licences Directive, or a driving licence recognised as equivalent.
(iii) See regulation 3(2) for vehicles to which these regulations DO NOT apply.
(iv) Being the holder of a certificate as required by the regulation may be evidenced by possession and production of any of the following:-
(a) a driver qualification card;
(b) a Community licence with the Community code;
(c) a driver's certificate granted to him/her by a member State as referred to in Article 10(3)(a) of Community Directive No 2003/59/EC; or
(d) any other document issued to the driver by a member State certifying an initial CPC or a periodic CPC .
(v) In England, Wales and Northern Ireland, "forges" means makes a false document in order that it may be used as genuine.
(vi) See regulation 13(5), (6), (7) and (8) for details in relation to the time limits on prosecutions.
(vii) In relation to proceedings in Scotland, section 136(3) of the Criminal Procedure (Scotland) Act 1995 (date of commencement of proceedings) shall apply for the purposes of this regulation as it applies for the purposes of that section.
(viii) See regulation 14 for the power to seize documents.
(ix) This offence no longer applies after the 2nd December 2024 due to changes made by SI 2024/1160 to the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007. For the offence applying after this date, see H101938.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 3 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit on prosecutions:
Complex - see regulation 13 of the Vehicle Drivers (Certificates of Professional Competence) Regulations 2007.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
